To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dysregulated expression c-myc induces PKD by promoting renal epithelial cell proliferation and apoptosis, which are independent of p53 and bcl- 2.
the c-myc gene induces polycystic kidneys in mice through a mechanism that is independent of the bcl2 and p53 genes.

1) the dysregulation of c-myc expression is sufficient to induce polycystic kidneys; 2) this c-myc-induced PKD is not associated with a significant increase in bcl- or p53 expression; and 3) c-myc-induced apoptosis is p53 and bcl- 2 independent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis for the development of renal cysts in polycystic disease, the commonest inherited human renal disorder.

the role of the c-myc proto-oncogene and its downstream targets in polycystic disease of the kidney, a genetic disorder that leads to end-stage renal failure and is the most common hereditary form of human renal disease.
the role of the c-Myc proto-oncogene in the development of polycystc kidney disease (PK).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
c-myc is a specific and critical factor for PKD pathogenesis, which occurs through a p-53 and bcl- 2–independent pathway.
the c-myc-induced apoptosis in polycystic kidneys is p53- and Bcl-2 independent.
the PKD in SBM mice is c-myc–dependent, p53- and Bcl-2-independent, and is associated with a significant elevation in renal cell apoptosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
c-Myc induces apoptosis by an intrinsic mechanism, which is independent of Bcl-2, Bax, and p53.
the pathogenesis and the progression of PKD is due to a c-Myc specific imbalance in cell proliferation and apoptosis.
the c-myc–induced renal cell proliferation in the SBM mouse is independent of p53 and bcl- 2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pathogenesis and the pathophysiology of PKD is not due to the loss of a tumor suppressor gene or the gain of a proto-oncogene, as has been suggested for other genetic diseases.
the c-myc gene can induce PKD through a p53-independent pathway, which may involve other members of the Bcl-2 protein family.
the dysregulated c-myc gene in PKD is a critical factor that promotes both epithelial proliferation and apoptosis.
